     1	# Plan v1 — #1615 cold-path-flooder multi-thread + mlx5 VF TX-queue distribution
     2	
     3	Closes #1615. Unblocks #1612 Scale Target table population and the
     4	downstream #1609 multi-stage-policy DAG plan-review.
     5	
     6	## 1. Problem statement
     7	
     8	The cold-path-flooder shipped in #1611 (squash `6c26c40e6`) is correct
     9	but caps at **~870 K pps single-thread** on `loss:cluster-userspace-host`,
    10	regardless of `--batch` (32 / 64 / 256) or `taskset -c 0` CPU pin.
    11	The #1611 plan v4 BLOCKING smoke gate is **≥2.5 Mpps**; that gate
    12	cannot be hit with the current single-thread design.
    13	
    14	This blocks #1612 Scale Target measurement table population (needs the
    15	flooder to actually saturate the cold path) which in turn blocks #1609
    16	multi-stage policy DAG v2 plan-review (needs the Scale Target numbers
    17	to size the DAG).
    18	
    19	## 2. Root cause — environment correction
    20	
    21	The #1615 issue body framed the ceiling as "container's virtio TX
    22	queue / qdisc=fq on IPVLAN". **That framing is wrong.** Inspection of
    23	the live container shows:
    24	
    25	- `cluster-userspace-host` is an Incus **container** (not a VM), not
    26	  virtio.
    27	- The container's `eth0` is a **direct SR-IOV VF** on parent `mlx1`
    28	  (line in `test/incus/cluster-setup.sh:485-492`), VLAN 3667:
    29	  ```yaml
    30	  devices.eth0:
    31	    nictype: sriov
    32	    parent: mlx1
    33	    vlan: "3667"
    34	  ```
    35	- `volatile.eth0.host_name: enp101s0f1v2` confirms it's an mlx5 VF
    36	  in the netns of the container (not bridged).
    37	- The VF in-container exposes **11 TX queues** (`/sys/class/net/eth0/queues/tx-{0..10}`).
    38	- The container has **16 CPUs** visible (`nproc`).
    39	- Qdisc on the VF is `fq` — but **`PACKET_QDISC_BYPASS=1`** is set in
    40	  the flooder (verified in `main.rs:734-751`), so qdisc is bypassed
    41	  on the TX path. The fq parent is not load-bearing for this ceiling.
    42	
    43	So the ~870 K pps ceiling is **not** virtio queue depth and **not**
    44	qdisc=fq serialization. The single-thread design pegs one CPU at a
    45	per-CPU softirq+mlx5_core xmit ceiling. The mlx5 VF can absorb much
    46	more aggregate pps; we are just under-feeding it with one TX-thread.
    47	
    48	### Why multi-thread breaks the ceiling
    49	
    50	`sendmmsg` on AF_PACKET SOCK_RAW with `PACKET_QDISC_BYPASS` calls
    51	`packet_direct_xmit` → driver `ndo_start_xmit` directly. The mlx5
    52	driver hashes by `skb_get_queue_mapping()` (set from skb hash of the
    53	5-tuple) to pick a TX queue. With one thread emitting from one socket
    54	with disjoint 5-tuples, the kernel still does:
    55	
    56	1. one `__local_bh_disable_ip()` per `sendmmsg` batch on the calling CPU
    57	2. one driver_xmit + completion path per packet, on the calling CPU
    58	3. skb alloc / kfree in the per-CPU slab cache on the calling CPU
    59	
    60	The calling CPU saturates around 870 K pps doing the skb alloc + driver
    61	xmit + completion. **Multiple threads on multiple CPUs let each one
    62	drive its own subset of the VF's 11 TX queues independently.**
    63	
    64	We expect ~4× when going from 1 to 4 threads (each on its own CPU),
    65	modulo mlx5 VF aggregate TX-PPS cap. 4 threads × 870 K = 3.48 Mpps,
    66	comfortably > 2.5 Mpps gate. If the VF caps at 2 Mpps aggregate this
    67	proves a separate ceiling, in which case PLAN-KILL is acceptable and
    68	the fallback is option 3 (PACKET_TX_RING) or option 1 (bare-metal
    69	generator).
    70	
    71	## 3. Design
    72	
    73	### 3.1 `--threads N` flag
    74	
    75	Add a `--threads N` flag to the flooder (default `1`, range `1..=16`).
    76	
    77	Per-thread state:
    78	- Own AF_PACKET SOCK_RAW socket (open + bind per-thread; do **not**
    79	  share fd, because Linux sendmmsg on AF_PACKET takes the socket
    80	  buffer lock; per-thread fd avoids the lock).
   120	Property test: spawn 4 threads with same `base_seed=1`; assert the
   121	first 1000 5-tuples generated by each thread are pairwise disjoint.
   122	
   123	### 3.4 Aggregate stats output
   124	
   125	Existing single-thread JSON summary shape preserved. Three new fields:
   126	- `"threads": N`
   127	- `"avg_pps": <aggregate>`  (sum across threads; this becomes the
   128	  smoke-gate metric)
   129	- `"per_thread": [ { "thread_id": 0, "avg_pps": X, "tx_packets": Y,
   130	  ... }, ... ]`
   131	
   132	Per-second progress lines on stderr each thread emits its own JSON
   133	with `"thread_id": T`. A final aggregated line is emitted by the main
   134	thread once per second (sum of last second's per-thread deltas).
   135	
   136	### 3.5 NOT in scope
   137	
   138	- PACKET_TX_RING / tpacket_v3: deferred again, per AGY r1's #1611
   139	  finding 2. Only revisit if multi-thread doesn't break ceiling.
   140	- Bare-metal generator (run flooder on loss host directly): out of
   141	  scope; that's a methodology change to docs/runbook, not a code
   142	  change.
   143	- Virtio queue tuning: N/A — container is on a direct mlx5 VF.
   144	- Frame size > 64: out of scope; this PR keeps the 64 B floor.
   145	- IPv6: out of scope; #1611 ships v4-only and #1612 measurement table
   146	  is v4-only.
   147	
   148	## 4. Files touched
   149	
   150	- `test/incus/cold-path-flooder/src/main.rs` — add `--threads`,
   340	## 11. References
   341	
   342	- #1611 plan v4: `docs/pr/1611-flooder-runner-body/plan-v4.md` (in
   343	  git history, on branch perf/1611-flooder-runner-body).
   344	- AGY r1 finding 2 on #1611 (PACKET_TX_RING deferred).
   345	- AGY r1 finding D on #1611 (cache-line align TxSlot).
   346	- Issue #1612 Scale Target measurement table — the dependent work
   347	  this PR unblocks.
   348	- `test/incus/cluster-setup.sh:474-538` — `create_lan_host()`, which
   349	  proves cluster-userspace-host is an SR-IOV container.

   200	            scheduler_name: String::new(),

   202	            source_literal_v4: PrefixSetV4::default(),
   203	            source_literal_v6: PrefixSetV6::default(),
   204	            destination_literal_v4: PrefixSetV4::default(),
   205	            destination_literal_v6: PrefixSetV6::default(),
   206	            source_book_idxs: SmallVec::new(),
   207	            destination_book_idxs: SmallVec::new(),
   208	            source_v4_match_any: true,
   209	            source_v6_match_any: true,
   210	            destination_v4_match_any: true,
   760	/// Composes (a) the literal CIDRs parsed for this side (passed in
   761	/// as `lit_vec`, already moved/owned) and (b) the prefixes from
   762	/// each cited address book on this side (looked up via the
   763	/// `extractor` closure that returns `&Arc<[T]>` for the
   764	/// appropriate family).
   765	///
   766	/// Returns `None` if and only if the union is empty (no literals,
   767	/// no cited-book contributions on this side+family). This is the
   768	/// canonical "any side" representation — paired with the existing
   769	/// `..._match_any` flag for semantic match shape.
   770	fn build_rule_side_arc<T: Clone, F>(
   771	    mut lit_vec: Vec<T>,
   772	    book_idxs: &SmallVec<[u32; 8]>,
   773	    books: &[BookEntry],
   774	    extractor: F,
   775	) -> Option<Arc<[T]>>
   776	where
   777	    F: Fn(&BookEntry) -> &Arc<[T]>,
   778	{
   779	    for &idx in book_idxs.iter() {
   780	        let book = &books[idx as usize];
   781	        lit_vec.extend_from_slice(extractor(book));
   782	    }
   783	    if lit_vec.is_empty() {
   784	        None
   785	    } else {
   786	        // Arc::from(Vec<T>) (impl since Rust 1.45) allocates a
   787	        // fresh Arc-headed slice and moves the items out of the
   788	        // Vec. Going via .into_boxed_slice() first would add a
   789	        // wasted shrink-to-fit realloc.
   790	        Some(Arc::from(lit_vec))
   791	    }
   792	}
   793	
   794	fn parse_literal_cidr_into(
   795	    prefix: &str,
   796	    out_v4: &mut Vec<PrefixV4>,
   797	    out_v6: &mut Vec<PrefixV6>,
   798	) {
   799	    if prefix.is_empty() || prefix == "any" {
   800	        return;
   801	    }
   802	    match prefix.parse::<IpNet>() {
   803	        Ok(IpNet::V4(net)) => out_v4.push(PrefixV4::from_net(net)),
   804	        Ok(IpNet::V6(net)) => out_v6.push(PrefixV6::from_net(net)),
   805	        Err(_) => {
   806	            if let Ok(ip) = prefix.parse::<Ipv4Addr>() {
   807	                out_v4.push(PrefixV4::from_net(
   808	                    ipnet::Ipv4Net::new(ip, 32).expect("v4 /32"),
   809	                ));
   810	            } else if let Ok(ip) = prefix.parse::<Ipv6Addr>() {
   811	                out_v6.push(PrefixV6::from_net(
   812	                    ipnet::Ipv6Net::new(ip, 128).expect("v6 /128"),
   813	                ));
   814	            }
   815	        }
   816	    }
   817	}
   818	
   819	fn resolve_book_idxs(
   820	    book_id_to_idx: &FxHashMap<u32, u32>,
   821	    ids: &[u32],
   822	    rule_id: &str,
   823	) -> Result<SmallVec<[u32; 8]>, SnapshotIntegrityError> {
   824	    let mut sorted = ids.to_vec();
   825	    sorted.sort_unstable();
   826	    sorted.dedup();
   827	    let mut out: SmallVec<[u32; 8]> = SmallVec::new();
   828	    for id in sorted {
   829	        let Some(&idx) = book_id_to_idx.get(&id) else {

  1001	fn parse_address(prefix: &str, out_v4: &mut Vec<PrefixV4>, out_v6: &mut Vec<PrefixV6>) {
  1002	    if prefix.is_empty() || prefix == "any" {
  1003	        return;
  1004	    }
  1005	    match prefix.parse::<IpNet>() {
  1006	        Ok(IpNet::V4(net)) => out_v4.push(PrefixV4::from_net(net)),
  1007	        Ok(IpNet::V6(net)) => out_v6.push(PrefixV6::from_net(net)),
  1008	        Err(_) => {
  1009	            if let Ok(ip) = prefix.parse::<Ipv4Addr>() {
  1010	                out_v4.push(PrefixV4::from_net(
  1011	                    ipnet::Ipv4Net::new(ip, 32).expect("v4 /32"),
  1012	                ));
  1013	            } else if let Ok(ip) = prefix.parse::<Ipv6Addr>() {
  1014	                out_v6.push(PrefixV6::from_net(
  1015	                    ipnet::Ipv6Net::new(ip, 128).expect("v6 /128"),
  1016	                ));
  1017	            }
  1018	        }
  1019	    }
  1020	}

    41	/// #1609 v3.1 Step 1 (STAGED scaffolding — narrow scope): the
    42	/// parallel `prefixes_v4` / `prefixes_v6` fields carry the
    43	/// canonical original prefix list for THIS book. Build code (a
    44	/// future Multi-Book LPM construction step) reads these directly
    45	/// without walking the `PrefixSetV{4,6}` trie. Hot-path
    46	/// `contains()` continues to use the existing `v4` / `v6`
    47	/// PrefixSets — these parallel fields are config-apply-time helpers
    48	/// only.
    49	///
    50	/// The two views agree by construction at the SEMANTIC
    51	/// (membership) level: `prefixes_v{4,6}` is the input Vec fed into
    52	/// `PrefixSetV{4,6}::from_v3_literals()` immediately after parsing
    53	/// the snapshot, so every IP that falls under any entry in
    54	/// `prefixes_v{4,6}` is also matched by `v{4,6}.contains()`. The
    55	/// two views are NOT structurally identical: PrefixSet may collapse
    56	/// to `MatchAny` when a /0 is present (dropping the non-/0 entries
    57	/// from its internal representation), and may build a Trie above
    58	/// `PREFIX_SET_LINEAR_MAX`. Tests assert the membership-equivalence
    59	/// property on representative inputs.
    60	///
    61	/// #1609 v3.1 scope discipline: this PR adds the field + parse-
    62	/// time population + unit test ONLY. The Multi-Book LPM that
    63	/// consumes these fields ships in a follow-up issue once the v3.2
    64	/// design round closes the remaining round-2 review findings.

   601	        // Precompute match-any flags. True iff EITHER the literal
   602	        // set OR any cited book's v4/v6 is MatchAny.
   603	        let source_v4_match_any = source_literal_v4.is_match_any()

   605	                .iter()
   606	                .any(|&i| state.books[i as usize].v4.is_match_any());

   615	        let destination_v6_match_any = destination_literal_v6.is_match_any()

   620	        // #1623 Path B narrow: materialize the parallel-prefix
   621	        // arrays. Each is the union of (a) the rule's own literal
   622	        // CIDRs and (b) every cited book's prefixes_v{4,6} on
   623	        // that side. Returns None when both sources are empty.
   624	        let source_prefixes_v4 = build_rule_side_arc(
   625	            src_lit_v4_vec,
   626	            &source_book_idxs,
   627	            &state.books,
   628	            |book| &book.prefixes_v4,
   629	        );
   630	        let source_prefixes_v6 = build_rule_side_arc(
   631	            src_lit_v6_vec,
   632	            &source_book_idxs,
   633	            &state.books,
   634	            |book| &book.prefixes_v6,
   635	        );
   636	        let destination_prefixes_v4 = build_rule_side_arc(
   637	            dst_lit_v4_vec,

   642	        let destination_prefixes_v6 = build_rule_side_arc(
   643	            dst_lit_v6_vec,
   644	            &destination_book_idxs,

   646	            |book| &book.prefixes_v6,
   647	        );
   648	
   649	        // #1623 Path B narrow: pre-declare applications +
   650	        // compiled_apps as locals so the struct literal can name
   651	        // every field explicitly — this drops the

   661	            policy_id: snap.policy_id,

   684	        };
   685	        let idx = state.rules.len();
   686	        let is_global = rule.from_zone == "junos-global" || rule.to_zone == "junos-global";
   687	        state.rules.push(rule);
   688

   690	            state.global_indices.push(idx);
   691	        } else {
   692	            match (
   693	                zone_name_to_id.get(&snap.from_zone).copied(),
   694	                zone_name_to_id.get(&snap.to_zone).copied(),

   699	                }
   700	                _ => {

   703	                        snap.from_zone, snap.to_zone
   704	                    );
   705	                }
   718	/// `Vec<PrefixV{4,6}>` alongside the PrefixSet so the caller can
   719	/// reuse them when populating the per-rule parallel prefix arrays.
   720	/// Cost: 2× `Vec::clone()` per rule on the parse path (cold). The
   721	/// alternative — threading `&mut Vec<...>` parameters through
   722	/// `PrefixSetV{4,6}::from_v3_literals` — is intrusive to the
   723	/// factory contract; the clone is acceptable per Codex r2/r3 +
   724	/// AGY r2/r3 cold-path approval.
   725	fn parse_v3_literal_set_capture(
   726	    literals: &[String],
   727	) -> (PrefixSetV4, PrefixSetV6, Vec<PrefixV4>, Vec<PrefixV6>) {
   728	    let mut any_v4 = false;
   729	    let mut any_v6 = false;
   730	    let mut v4: Vec<PrefixV4> = Vec::new();
   731	    let mut v6: Vec<PrefixV6> = Vec::new();
   732	    for tok in literals {
   733	        match tok.as_str() {
   734	            "any" => {
   735	                any_v4 = true;
   736	                any_v6 = true;
   737	            }
   738	            "any4" => any_v4 = true,
   739	            "any6" => any_v6 = true,
   740	            "" => {}
   741	            s => parse_literal_cidr_into(s, &mut v4, &mut v6),
   742	        }
   743	    }
   744	    let v4_set = if any_v4 {
   745	        PrefixSetV4::MatchAny
   746	    } else {
   747	        PrefixSetV4::from_v3_literals(v4.clone())
   748	    };
   749	    let v6_set = if any_v6 {
   750	        PrefixSetV6::MatchAny
   751	    } else {
   752	        PrefixSetV6::from_v3_literals(v6.clone())
   753	    };
   754	    (v4_set, v6_set, v4, v6)
   755	}

     1	# Claude SMR plan-review r1 — #1608 v3 (research)
     2	
     3	**Reviewer:** Claude SMR (domain SMR + CPU arch/design + SW design patterns)
     4	**Posture:** HOSTILE. The history (v1 6-fatal kill, v2 10-fatal kill) is a
     5	strong prior that the design surface is deep and a soft pass is wrong.
     6	**Verdict:** **PLAN-KILL-CONFIRMED** (Path A), with Path D as the reopen
     7	criterion. The plan's own recommendation is correct; I verified the
     8	load-bearing claims against `origin/master @ 6bdf9d73e` and they hold.
     9	
    10	## Verified factual claims (with line evidence)
    11	
    12	### Claim: neg_neigh gate fires before policy eval for unresolved dst — TRUE
    13	`poll_descriptor/mod.rs:2392` `ForwardingDisposition::MissingNeighbor =>`
    14	opens the arm; `:2418` `let fast_fail = neg_neigh_gate(...)`; `:2433-2442`
    15	`if fast_fail { ... binding.scratch.scratch_recycle.push(desc.addr);
    16	continue; }`. The `continue` (`:2442`) skips the session-install policy
    17	eval at `:2522` (`evaluate_policy_with_len`). So a negatively-cached,
    18	unresolved, un-expired dst never reaches policy eval. **#1660 genuinely
    19	short-circuits the dead-host flood class before the policy scan.**
    20	
    21	### Claim: live/resolved dst still hits policy eval every cold packet — TRUE
    22	The canonical new-flow policy decision is at `:1393`
    23	`evaluate_policy_result_with_len(...)` in the ForwardCandidate slow path,
    24	which is NOT the MissingNeighbor arm and never consults `neg_neigh`. A
    25	flood to a resolvable dst (the victim service, or the firewall's own
    26	on-link subnet) reaches `:1393` per packet. **This is the only residual
    27	threat #1608 uniquely addresses** — Section 4's table is accurate.
    28	
    29	### Claim: cold path is still a linear zone-pair scan post-#1606 — TRUE
    30	`policy.rs:885-899`: `if let Some(indices) = state.zone_pair_index.get(&key)
    31	{ for &idx in indices { ... try_match_rule(&state.rules[idx], ...) } }`.
    32	`try_match_rule` (`policy.rs:926`) does the inactive gate, then
    33	`compiled_apps.matches` (O(1)), then `policy.rs:944-949`
    34	`source_v4_match_any || source_literal_v4.contains(src) ||
    35	source_book_idxs.iter().any(|&i| state.books[i as usize].v4.contains(src))`.
    36	Address-book bodies are shared via `state.books` (the #1606 dedup); the
    37	rule-count-linear part is the outer `for &idx in indices`. **The plan's
    38	Section 2 topology is exact.**
    39	
    40	### Claim: #1623 DAG never shipped; only scaffolding — TRUE
    41	`policy.rs:182-185` carries `source_prefixes_v{4,6}: Option<Arc<[PrefixV4]>>`
    42	with a doc comment (`:170-181`) stating "NOT consumed by the hot path in
    43	this PR (zero-touch on `evaluate_policy`)". The multi-stage DAG is absent
    44	from `evaluate_policy_result_with_len`. **The chartered fix for the
    45	rule-count-linear cost (#1609/#1623) was PLAN-KILLED; the cost remains.**
    46	
    47	### Claim: cold-path bottleneck unmeasured — TRUE
    48	`docs/userspace-jit-design.md` "Measurement plan" (~:639) lists the

    53	magnitude below the ~5 Mpps/worker cold-path saturation. **The cold path

   548	    hist:    [[u64; HIST_BUCKETS]; ZP_SLOTS],
   549	    sum_ns:  [u64; ZP_SLOTS],
   550	    samples: [u64; ZP_SLOTS],
   551	    /// Sum of zone_pair_keys that landed in each slot, used by the
   552	    /// reader to flag aliasing.  (At most 16 keys per slot in default
   553	    /// K=16 config → no collision.)
   554	    keys_seen_xor: [u32; ZP_SLOTS],
   555	}
   556	
   557	#[repr(align(64))]
   558	pub(in crate::afxdp) struct WorkerColdPathAtomics {
   559	    hist:    [[AtomicU64; HIST_BUCKETS]; ZP_SLOTS],
   560	    sum_ns:  [AtomicU64; ZP_SLOTS],
   561	    samples: [AtomicU64; ZP_SLOTS],
   562	    keys_seen_xor: [AtomicU64; ZP_SLOTS],  // u64 for atomic uniformity
   563	}
   564	```
   565	
   566	Bucket layout note: with 24 buckets, the saturation edge is **2^32 ns
   567	≈ 4.295 s** (any `ns ≥ 2^32` maps to bucket 23). AGY r2 axis 4 caught
   568	the earlier prose claim of "saturates at 2^33 ns" — that was wrong;
   569	the math is `b = (54 - clz(ns|1)).max(0).min(23)`. For our worst-case
   570	projection of 1M-rule linear scan at ~100 ns/rule = ~100 ms per packet
   571	(~10^8 ns ≈ 2^27 ns), the result lands in bucket ~17 — well below
   572	saturation. Tail is visible.
   573	
   574	Size per worker: 16 × 24 × 8 + 16 × 8 × 3 = 3072 + 384 = **3456 B**
   575	per worker, ~54 cache lines. With 6 workers = 20.7 KB total. Cheap
   576	in absolute terms; localized to one struct so a future redesign
   577	(e.g. per-zone-pair flat array indexed by id) doesn't need to touch
   578	the call sites.
   579	
   580	Publish path: per-tick (`~1 Hz`) the worker calls
   581	`WorkerColdPathAtomics::publish(&counters)`; 24 × 16 + 3 × 16 = 432
   582	Relaxed stores per worker per second. Negligible.
   583	
   584	### 4.5 CPU isolation recording (harness side)
   585	
   586	AGY r2 hazard 2: the LAN_HOST container (`cluster-userspace-host`)
   587	runs on the same physical loss host as `xpf-userspace-fw0` with no
   588	explicit CPU pinning. Under heavy flooder load (5+ Mpps random-source
   589	generation) the host scheduler can co-locate flooder threads on the
   590	same physical cores as FW0 worker threads, introducing per-run

   332	// doesn't drop frames. PendingNeighPacket is 264 B on x86_64 (XdpDesc +
   333	// UserspaceDpMeta + SessionDecision + flow key + queued_ns + probe_attempts),
   334	// so worst-case per binding when the queue is fully populated is ~1.0 MiB.
   335	// To avoid paying that ~1.0 MiB up front per binding × N bindings, the
   336	// underlying VecDeque is now constructed with `VecDeque::new()` (zero
   337	// capacity) at worker init — see worker/mod.rs.
   338	// The buffer grows on push only when traffic actually queues up, and the
   339	// 4096 admission check in poll_descriptor.rs enforces the upper bound.
   340	// This unblocks parallel-connect storms during cluster failback while
   341	// keeping idle-binding RSS near zero.
   342	const MAX_PENDING_NEIGH: usize = 4096;
   343	
   344	// #1651 B3: dead-host negative neighbor cache (per binding). When a
   345	// pending_neigh entry times out after best-effort ARP/NDP probes without
   346	// resolving, its (egress_ifindex, next_hop) is recorded here so subsequent
   347	// cold packets to the same dead host fast-fail immediately (recycle, no
   348	// pending_neigh slot consumed) instead of each buffering a SYN for the full
   349	// PENDING_NEIGH_TIMEOUT. This is the AGY-r1 HIGH starvation defense: a
   350	// dead-host SYN storm can no longer saturate the bounded pending_neigh queue
   351	// and drop LIVE cold connects at the full-queue gate.
   352	//
   353	// NEG_NEIGH_TTL_NS = 3 s: (a) > the 800 ms fast drop so each storm packet is
   354	// suppressed across many connection attempts; (b) short enough that a
   355	// recovered-but-silent host is penalized at most one TTL window. A host that
   356	// actually recovers AND receives traffic is evicted immediately by the
   357	// resolved-neighbor-wins check in poll_descriptor (RTM_NEWNEIGH populates the
   358	// shared dynamic_neighbors), so the TTL only governs recovered-but-silent
   359	// destinations.
   360	const NEG_NEIGH_TTL_NS: u64 = 3_000_000_000; // 3 seconds
   361	// Per-binding cap on the negative cache. A /24 scan touches 254 distinct
   362	// dsts; 256 covers a full subnet sweep without unbounded growth. On overflow
   363	// the map is cleared wholesale — a best-effort optimization, so losing
   364	// suppression for a few dsts only costs one more PENDING_NEIGH_TIMEOUT drop,
   365	// never correctness. FastMap::clear() retains bucket capacity (no realloc).
